summary: The tested UI is visually isomorphic: the textarea border, text wrapping, character counter, validation message, colors, spacing, and error state match on both ends.
The comparison canvases differ: Android is manually cropped to 342×252 component bounds, while iOS is an uncropped 1170×2532 full-screen capture with substantial blank space below the component.
The top-right harness badge differs in content and width, reading "ANDROID" on the left and "IOS" on the right.
likelyCauses: The baseline and current captures use different crop contracts; current has no crop applied.
The platform badge is a Slock/Kuikly harness overlay populated from the rendering platform.
suggestedFixes: Apply the same component-bounds crop and device-pixel-ratio normalization to both captures before comparison.
Exclude or normalize the platform badge overlay when validating the textarea component itself.
intentional: The "ANDROID" versus "IOS" badge text is an expected platform indicator rather than a component-state difference.

summary: No actionable visual divergence is visible: the Android and iOS skeletons match in element count, dimensions, alignment, spacing, corner radius, and fill after normalizing capture scale.
Header typography and component placement match, with no missing elements, clipping, or inconsistent state indicators.
cases.suggestedOwner: UiSkeleton component owners; no defect action is required
suggestedFixes: No UI correction is required; retain the current shared skeleton styling and layout parameters.
Normalize future comparisons to equivalent component bounds and scale to avoid raw-resolution and crop noise.
intentional: The skeleton content stack intentionally overflows into the bottom padding of the fixed 150 px canvas to mirror the documented React/CSS behavior; the residual sub-pixel overflow is not a defect.

summary: The Android capture is cropped to the 390×60 tab-bar component bounds, while the iOS capture remains a full 1170×2532 screen, leaving a large blank region below the component.
Within the tab bar, item order, spacing, iconography, typography, selected-state treatment, and colors appear equivalent, with no visible missing elements or clipping.
likelyCauses: Asymmetric Slock crop configuration: the baseline uses a manual component-bounds rectangle, while the current capture has no crop.
The Android and iOS runners emitted different screenshot canvas sizes for the same fixture.
suggestedFixes: Apply the same component-bounds crop to the iOS capture, or normalize both captures to the same logical 390×60 region before comparison.
Keep full-screen captures as separate artifacts and exclude the empty iOS viewport area from the component-level diff.
intentional: The documented Android ALL-CAPS tab-label convention versus Title Case labels, and any route-derived difference in the selected tab, are intentional platform differences and should not be normalized.

summary: The application UI is visually isomorphic: message bounds, selection states, typography hierarchy, wrapping, spacing, colors, avatars, reactions, and the bottom action bar match.
The only visible divergence is the comparison-frame badge at the top right: the left badge reads “ANDROID” and has a wider bound than the right badge reading “iOS”.
likelyCauses: The platform badge is injected by the Slock comparison harness rather than rendered by the shared application UI.
The reported 1.66% pixel mismatch is below the configured 2% tolerance and may include minor platform rasterization/antialiasing differences.
suggestedFixes: No application parity fix is required.
If the comparison should cover product UI only, mask or crop the platform badge to prevent intentional label and width differences from affecting results.
intentional: The top-right Android-versus-iOS platform badge is expected to differ in both label and width.

summary: Android renders a loaded member profile, while iOS renders a full-page "Could not load member" error state.
The headers differ: Android shows the artin avatar, "artin", "@artin", and a member-management icon; iOS shows "Member" and "Profile" with none of those elements.
Android displays the avatar, name, handle, "(you)" badge, Description/Owner, Info, Role, Email, Joined, and Created Agents sections; all are absent on iOS.
iOS uniquely shows a centered warning triangle, error message, and outlined Retry button; Android shows no error or retry controls.
likelyCauses: The iOS member-detail request failed or returned no usable data.
The platforms may be using different member identifiers, API routes, fixtures, or mock data.
The iOS response mapping or decoding may be failing for the member payload.
Platform-specific loading and error handling is sending iOS into the error state while Android loads successfully.
cases.suggestedOwner: iOS client team responsible for member-profile data fetching and screen state
suggestedFixes: Run both platforms against the same successful member fixture and compare the requested member identifier and endpoint.
Inspect iOS network and decoding logs for the member request and correct any response-mapping or route differences.
Restore the shared success-state layout on iOS: member header, avatar, name, handle, self badge, member action, and all profile sections.
Verify that iOS only shows the full-page error and Retry action when loading genuinely fails, not because of platform-specific fixture or state handling.
Rerun the visual comparison with equivalent viewport dimensions and the same member data.

summary: Capture framing is materially different: Android is 390×1901, while iOS is 1170×2532, nominally 390×844 CSS px at 3× DPR.
The iOS capture ends midway through the Runtime config section, clipping the "Reasoning" label. Android continues with Reasoning, Mode, Environment variables, Skills, Agent migration, and Actions.

Android shows the complete Actions block, including Stop agent, Restart / reset, Copy diagnostic info, Report issue, and Archive agent; these controls are absent from the iOS frame because they are outside its captured extent.
likelyCauses: Android appears to use a full-page capture while iOS uses a viewport-only capture.
The iOS scrollable content area was not expanded to its full height before capture.
Screenshot density and crop policy differ: Android is effectively 1× with a manual crop, while iOS is 3× and uncropped.
cases.suggestedOwner: Kuikly mobile screenshot and visual-testing pipeline
suggestedFixes: Use the same capture mode and CSS viewport dimensions for both platforms, preferably full-page capture or equivalent scroll-segment capture.
Normalize the 1170×2532 iOS image to its 390 CSS-px logical width and apply equivalent crop bounds to both images.
Capture iOS with a full-height page or scroll container so Runtime config, Skills, Agent migration, and Actions are included.
Rerun the comparison with matching capture policies before treating the unseen iOS sections as missing UI.
